body_ar:
من أعظم صفات الله صفة الاستواء وصفة النزول إلى السماء الدنيا، وصفة العلو والفوقية، وأهل السنة يثبتونها بلا تشبيه ولا تعطيل، وقد ضل فيها المشبهة والمعطلة.
من صفات الله الفعلية.
إثبات صفة الاستواء لله جل وعلا:
يقول الشيخ حفظه الله: [قد استوى إلى السماء واستوى بعد على العرش بخلف المحتوى] هذه صفة أخرى هي صفة الاستواء وهي من الصفات الفعلية، وهي على نوعين: النوع الأول: المعدى بإلى، والنوع الثاني: المعدى بعلى فالنوع الأول: المعدى بإلى، جاء في السماء في قوله: ثُمَّ اسْتَوَى إِلَى السَّمَاءِ وَهِيَ دُخَانٌ فَقَالَ لَهَا وَلِلأَرْضِ اِئْتِيَا طَوْعاً أَوْ كَرْهاً قَالَتَا أَتَيْنَا طَائِعِينَ [فصلت:11] والاستواء المعدى بإلى هو بمعنى التوجه والنظر، وأما الاستواء المعدى بعلى فمعناه الاستقرار والثبات. وأما استواء الله سبحانه وتعالى على عرشه فلا يفسر، فهو من الصفات الثابتة التي قراءتها تفسيرها ولا يجوز تفسيرها بأي شيء؛ لأننا لا علم لنا بهذا؛ فلهذا من فسره بما فسرنا به الاستواء في اللغة فقد ابتدع، فمن قال: استوى على العرش بمعنى: استقر عليه أو نحو هذا فقد ابتدع في دين الله، فلم يرد هذا عن أحد...
body_en:
*[Site synopsis]* Among the greatest of God's attributes are the attribute of rising (istiwāʾ), the attribute of descending to the lowest heaven, and the attribute of highness and aboveness. The People of the Sunnah affirm them without likening God to creation and without divesting Him of His attributes, while the anthropomorphists and those who divest Him of His attributes have gone astray concerning them.

## Some of God's active attributes

## Affirming the attribute of rising for God, majestic and exalted

The Sheikh, may God preserve him, says:

*[He rose towards the heaven, and He rose thereafter over the Throne — with a difference in what is contained.]*

This is another attribute, the attribute of rising, and it is one of the active attributes. It is of two kinds: the first, the kind governed by the preposition "towards" (ilā); the second, the kind governed by the preposition "over" (ʿalā).

The first kind, governed by "towards", comes with respect to the heaven, in His words: {Then He rose towards the heaven while it was smoke, and said to it and to the earth: Come, willingly or unwillingly. They said: We come willingly} (Sūrat Fuṣṣilat 41:11). Rising governed by "towards" has the sense of turning to and regarding. As for rising governed by "over", its meaning is settling and fixity.

As for the rising of God, glorified and exalted is He, over His Throne, it is not interpreted. It is one of the established attributes whose recitation is their interpretation, and it is not permissible to interpret it by anything whatever, because we have no knowledge of this. For this reason, whoever interprets it by what we have interpreted rising by in the language has innovated. So whoever says "He rose over the Throne" in the sense of "He settled upon it", or anything of that sort, has innovated in the religion of God, for nothing of this has come down from anyone…

flags.note: Excerpt only, style guide section 9. The full lesson sits behind /medias/doc/esmawesivat-11.doc. The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends and completes nothing. Must not be rendered as a whole lesson.

flags.arabic: الفقرة الافتتاحية مقابل ما بعد العنوان الفرعي
flags.context: the synopsis paragraph against the transcribed commentary
options: mark the synopsis as the site's own and the remainder as the Sheikh's words
present the whole record as the Sheikh's words
flags.note: The record has more than one author. The opening paragraph is a synopsis written by the site, speaking about the lesson in the third person; everything from the section heading onward is the lecturer's own words as transcribed, together with the quoted line of the versified base text, which is his teacher's. The site must keep the voices apart.

flags.context: the two groups the rule is framed to answer
options: the anthropomorphists (al-Mushabbihah) / those who divest God of His attributes (al-Muʿaṭṭilah)
the likeners / the deniers of the attributes
flags.note: Both are polemical labels for theological opponents, not self-descriptions of any surviving school, and neither has a settled English equivalent. Rendered descriptively and kept identical across the whole 734-747 run so the series reads consistently. The Sheikh's office should fix a single pair of renderings for the corpus.

flags.arabic: فمن قال: استوى على العرش بمعنى: استقر عليه أو نحو هذا فقد ابتدع في دين الله
flags.context: the close of the excerpt, on interpreting God's rising over the Throne
options: translate faithfully and hold for editorial decision
flags.note: Style guide section 12, and the single most consequential sentence in this run. The Sheikh here rules that glossing istiwāʾ ʿalā al-ʿarsh as 'settling upon' is innovation in religion (bidʿah). That gloss is held and taught by identifiable living scholars and institutions, so in English the sentence reads as a named charge against them. It is translated exactly, neither softened nor strengthened; 'ابتدع' is rendered 'has innovated' and not 'has committed heresy'. Whether and how to publish belongs to Ummah Collective and the Sheikh's office.

flags.context: فهو من الصفات الثابتة التي قراءتها تفسيرها ولا يجوز تفسيرها بأي شيء
options: it is not permissible to interpret it
it is rationally impossible to interpret it
flags.note: The kalām exemption of style guide section 8 does NOT apply here, and the first option is correct. The subject of 'يجوز' is a human act — interpreting — and not a proposition about God, so this is the legal sense (jāʾiz / permissible) and not rational possibility. Flagged because the surrounding material is creedal and a reader applying section 8 mechanically would get this backwards.

flags.context: قد استوى إلى السماء واستوى بعد على العرش بخلف المحتوى
options: with a difference in what is contained
with a difference in the content
with a difference in what is comprised
flags.note: The hemistich is elliptical and the Sheikh never glosses it before the record stops; on the most natural reading it marks that the two risings differ in meaning, which is exactly what the prose then goes on to argue. The literal rendering is kept rather than the paraphrase the prose would license, since the prose is the commentary and not the line.

translator_notes: One of a run of fourteen records, IDs 734-747, the series 'The Names and Attributes', all built to the same template and all excerpts. Each carries a site-written synopsis, then a section heading, then the opening formula and the first lines of a lesson, and then breaks off on an ellipsis; the full text sits behind a .doc download in the /medias/doc/esmawesivat-* series, numbered 1 to 14 in the same order as the IDs.

The source's final line, 'تحميل المادة' ('download the material'), is the label of a download link in the page furniture, not part of the text. It is recorded as source_download_link and omitted from body_ar and body_en.

This record does carry a CMS timestamp in a .create_date span (10 May 2011, within a 28-minute window shared by the whole run 738-747). That is a bulk-upload timestamp for the series, not the date the lesson was given. Record 737, translated in an earlier wave, reports no date for this run; the timestamp is in fact present in the page and should be backfilled there.
Qur'anic renderings here are interpretive and are not a substitute for the Arabic.

Creedal material. Per style guide section 8, the vocabulary of divine attributes is not the vocabulary of the five legal rulings, and the five-rulings mapping is not applied to any predicate of God in this record.

The synopsis announces three attributes — rising, descending to the lowest heaven, and highness and aboveness. Only the first is reached. Marked critical_for_display, and with unusual force here: the excerpt ends on a charge of innovation, which is the last thing a reader sees, and whatever qualification the Sheikh gave it is in the .doc.

'استوى' is rendered throughout as 'rose' rather than 'ascended', 'established Himself' or 'mounted'. Each of the alternatives commits to one of the interpretations the Sheikh is here refusing to make, which would invert the passage.

'الصفات الثابتة التي قراءتها تفسيرها' is rendered literally, 'the established attributes whose recitation is their interpretation'. It is a known formula of the discipline (associated with the reply attributed to Malik) and the Sheikh gives it without attribution, so none is supplied.
